messages:
andy: Heads-up — running long-context load tests on recent runtime build and KV cache memory keeps creeping. Not classic leak, looks like fragmentation + small-block churn.
megan: Ugh. Is this on the quantized path or fp16?
and y: (typo)
andy: fp16 path, but same behavior on q4_0 runs. Growth mostly after sequences > 64k tokens.
samir: Any allocator metrics (active vs resident vs mapped)?
andy: Yep. vmstats: RSS increases steadily, malloc_active up, but huge gap to malloc_total. Fragmentation ratio ~1.7 after a few hours.
megan: Do we have jemalloc stats from the perf build?
andy: Attached snippet from /proc/self/smaps and je-ctl:
```
Arena 0: mapped=1.2G allocated=720M active=420M
small blocks: count=124k free=58k
large chunks: count=44 free=12
fragmentation estimate: 1.7
```
megan: Sounds like a lot of small free blocks not getting reused. Could be our per-request KV sizes vary and we aren't coalescing.
lucia: Are we using fixed slab sizes or variable allocations? I thought the KV arena uses 4KB blocks currently.
andy: Implementation currently rounds entries to nearest 4KB and uses freelists per slab. That was to make indexing simple.
samir: 4KB granularity is probably too coarse for short-kv items and too fine for big KV from long prompts. Leads to internal fragmentation both ways.
megan: Could we try 1KB block size for small profiles and 64KB for large? Hybrid allocator?
andy: That's the idea. Two proposals we discussed earlier: (A) multi-class slab allocator (1KB/4KB/16KB/64KB) with compaction between classes; (B) keep current but add background compactor that merges adjacent free blocks into larger free ranges.
samir: Compactor sounds safer for short-term, but it's heavier CPU and tricky with live KV pointers. We need safe pointer swizzling or copy-on-evict.
lucia: Another angle: reuse policy — LRU vs MRU. Right now eviction is per-sequence LRU; but high churn sequences create many small frees that never match future sequences. Maybe use size-aware reuse: prefer reusing blocks of same size class.
andy: Correct — current freelist is global per size class but we don't track last-used-model or token-range. So cross-model fragmentation occurs.
megan: Do we have profiling traces linking allocation patterns to specific models or requests?
andy: Yes. I ran heap profiles with pprof and flamegraphs. Most churn comes from chat-style rerolls that append short deltas ~800B and then long context reads. After a while, free bins pile up with 1–2KB holes.
samir: For the long-term, multi-class slab + background compaction with pointer indirection sounds robust: store KV entries via small handle that points to slab+offset. Compaction copies live entries and updates handles. Overhead is an extra indirection but reduces fragmentation.
lucia: We should measure the perf hit for handle indirection on hot-path token generation. Even a 1–2% latency increase might be acceptable if memory goes down 30–50%.
megan: Can we add an adaptive block size tuner? Runtime observes distribution of sizes and adjusts slab thresholds and compaction cadence.
andy: I mocked a simple tuner: every 10 minutes sample allocation histogram, if > 60% of allocations under 2KB, start splitting 4KB slabs into 1KB pools gradually. It reduced fragmentation in the experiment by ~35% and RSS stabilized.
infra-bot: Auto-eviction: model/gpt-xyz eviction triggered on host gpu-09 at 2026-03-03T14:03:40Z (reason: oom_guard).
andy: Note: splitting slabs immediately increased CPU usage by ~8% due to more freelist ops. But request p50 didn't move. p99 widened by ~12ms in a few configs.
samir: That tradeoff might be OK for Dedicated customers on high-density hosts. But for hosted latency-sensitive routes we need fallback: dynamic policy per-route.
lucia: For compaction safety: we can quiesce an arena, stop mutating producers, run compaction, then resume. For live serving that's disruptive. So incremental compaction with read-copy-update + handle swap is safer.
megan: Can we prototype a background worker that compacts one slab page at a time and records mapping updates in a per-shard update log? Then writers apply updates lazily.
andy: That's what I prototyped. Worker copies live entries to new page, appends mapping entries, then flips the handle in an atomic compare-and-swap. Writers see new handle on next access. Works but needs double-write during compaction for updated entries.
samir: Also need to ensure KV cache TTL semantics — entries shouldn't be promoted during compaction incorrectly. Test cases needed.
lucia: Action items:
- andy: push prototype of multi-class slab + simple tuner to branch kv/allocator-tuner (include perf harness)
- megan: add jemalloc->tcmalloc comparison run and collect fragmentation metrics across both
- samir: design compaction safe-swap sequence and write unit tests for handle consistency
- lucia: run long-context 24h load with realistic chat traces and capture pprof + jemalloc stats every 30m

megan: Also add a telemetry counter for small-block-fill-rate and compaction-saves to console so we can correlate with rollouts.
andy: Will do. I'll post branch and a short readme with how to reproduce the run.
samir: Thx. If the tuner + slabs buy us 30% less RSS with <5% p99 cost we can roll as opt-in flag.
lucia: If anyone wants to pair on the compaction design ping me — I can help with correctness tests.
megan: Great thread. Let's keep this thread for coordination. :white_check_mark:
